notes.note: Titan does not implement encvalue_o/decvalue_o (applies to all C.05.05 and C.05.06 accept tests of this batch). All four parameters are passed (bit_length follows the defaulted ones); note the BNF in 16.1.2 lists only three arguments for encvalue_o, inconsistent with the C.5.5 signature. Mapping the calls to encvalue/decvalue, Titan only objects to an explicit "" dynamic_encoding, which is the documented default value.

Uses a 5-bit bitstring with encode "RAW"/FIELDLENGTH(5) to obtain a non-octet-aligned encoding; the codec and variant are tool-specific. The check (encvalue bits are the leading bits of encvalue_o) holds generally; vacuous if the codec pads to octets. Same for test_007 (padding bits are 0).
Ambiguity: mandatory reading chosen, bit_length is passed as fourth actual parameter and compared with lengthof(encvalue(...)).
Tests the 27.9 rule that the selection is applied recursively to fields (nested type with two encode attributes). Codec tests in this batch assume JSON/XML codecs exist for the types.
Invalid JSON input 'FFFEFDFC'O is assumed to give the unspecified failure 1; the exact code is codec dependent.
Conflict: 16.1.2 a)3 lists only decvalue/decvalue_unichar as allowing an uninitialized encoded_value, but C.5.6 specifies result 1 for decvalue_o; the C.5.6 reading is tested.
Truncated encoding (first half of the octets) is assumed to give result 2; codec dependent.
Uses send restriction 22.2.1 b) (type of in-line template must be given if ambiguous), distinct from the specific-value rule tested in test_003.
Observed from the module control function: a test case using rnd between two control rnd calls does not disturb the control sequence.
Ambiguity: literal reading chosen, rnd() after rnd(0.5)=r equals rnd(r).
PTC seeds its generator, waits while the MTC reseeds its own, then its next value must equal the reference sequence; timer-based interleaving.
